title: Icon Language
description: Versioned design rules that every icon in a set must follow. Top-level tokens describe the default optical size; `sizes` adds more.

grid.description: Layout grid for element boxes. Not a pixel-snapping rule.

trim.description: Inset from the canvas edge that no ink may cross. Between safeArea and this is the padding a stroke may overhang into. Defaults to 0, the canvas edge.

stroke.description: Cap and join may be omitted: absent means derived from the personality axes. Width has no derivation, so it must be stated.

cornerRadius.description: Omit to derive from the personality axes. Present means an override that wins.

filled.description: Which icons this product needs a filled version of. A policy, not a rule: coverage is reported and a person decides.

requiredFor.description: Concept tags whose icons need a filled version.

minNegativeSpace.description: Minimum visible gap between shapes of different elements. 0 disables.

minCutout.description: Narrowest knock-out that still reads in the filled style. Omit to use one stroke width at this size.

sizes.description: Additional optical sizes. Unspecified fields inherit from the default size.

trim.description: Inset from the canvas edge that no ink may cross. Scaled from the primary size when omitted.

minCutout.description: Narrowest knock-out that still reads in the filled style. Omit to use one stroke width at this size.

optics.description: Overrides for this size. Absent, the notch scales with the canvas and the ratios carry over unchanged.

preferences.description: Weight per scored preference, by rule id (restraint, balance, symmetry, silhouette, breathing). Absent means 1; 0 turns one off. Which preferences matter is taste, and taste is the team's.

optical.description: Keyline boxes per optical shape. Defaults derive from canvas and safe area.

character.description: Why the icons look the way they do. Consumed by the studio, the docs and any drafting agent.

axes.description: 0–100 between named poles: geometric (organic→geometric), minimal (expressive→minimal), technical (friendly→technical), literal (abstract→literal).

grammar.description: How icons are constructed. Checkable by the validator and followed by layout recipes.

angles.description: Allowed straight-line angles, measured 0–180. Empty means any angle.

arrangements.description: How this set draws each way of relating parts. A concept asking for an arrangement this set does not allow is refused.

spacing.description: Gap between units in a stack or a row, in units at the primary size. 0 means use the language's minimum gap.

optics.description: Optical corrections, applied at render and never at validation. Every one is off by default: a correction changes icons that are already published, so opting in has to be a decision somebody made.

junctionNotch.description: Trim a stroke end back from a junction it meets at an acute angle, in units at this optical size. 0 disables the pass.

junctionAngle.description: At or below this angle, in degrees, a junction counts as acute. Default 45.

interiorThin.description: Fraction by which to thin a stroke drawing detail inside another shape of the same element, so the outer contour stays the heavier line. 0 disables the pass.

dotRatio.description: Drawn diameter of a dot, as a multiple of stroke width. 0 disables the pass.

axisEndpoints.description: What one personality axis moves, and the token value at each of its two poles. The axis position interpolates between them, the way a variable font interpolates a weight axis.

cornerRadius.description: [value at 0, value at 100], as a fraction of the canvas.

derivation.description: What each personality axis moves, and to what value at each pole. Editing this is how a team says what "minimal" means for their set rather than inheriting ours. Where two axes move the same token, the proposal is the mean of their contributions.

construction.description: How a part is built, as opposed to how big or how heavy it is. A trait is a named decision that several primitives consume, so setting one changes every primitive that declared it and nothing else. Traits are ratios, so unlike the size tokens they do not vary per optical size. Omit one to derive it from the personality axes.

interiorRadius.description: How much of the exterior corner radius an interior corner takes. 0 is square and is the default, which is what Google and IBM both specify; 1 follows the silhouette, which is what Material's Rounded family does.

grade.description: Thickness offset applied only on a dark ground, as a fraction of stroke width. Negative thins. A light shape on a dark ground reads heavier than the same shape inverted; Material Symbols ships the GRAD axis for exactly this.

aperture.description: How an opening is drawn. "mixed" is not a style but an unmade decision: each part keeps the answer it was drawn with, which is what preserves a set that currently answers the question more than one way.

inset.description: Multiplier on how far interior detail sits from the contour it is inside. 1 leaves each part as drawn.

accentSize.description: Multiplier on the signature round part: a head, a wheel, the dot of a pin. 1 leaves each part as drawn.

slope.description: The pitch of a sloping or receding plane. "mixed" keeps each part as drawn.

exceptions.description: Per-part departures from the traits above, keyed by primitive name. Allowed, because forbidding what you cannot fully judge gets worked around in worse ways. Never silent: a reason is required, and the set-level audit counts them. One is a judgement; several on one trait means the language value is wrong.

set.description: Traits this part departs on. Anything absent still follows the language.

why.description: What was seen that the language value got wrong. Required: an exception without a reason is drift with a nicer name.

corners.description: Radius bands, sharpest corner first. The last band omits `upTo` and takes everything above the one before.

upTo.description: Applies to corners at or below this included angle, in degrees.

radius.description: Radius as a multiple of the size's cornerRadius.

cornerSnap.description: Pull each rounded corner to a radius whose tangent points land on the layout grid.
